messages.content: Can you retrieve the weather forecast for White Plains for next week with temperatures in Celsius?

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

We need to find the latitude and longitude for White Plains. White Plains is a city in New York, USA. Coordinates: approx 41.0536° N, 73.7629° W. So latitude ~41.0536, longitude ~-73.7629. We want forecast for next week. The Open-Meteo API supports daily forecasts. We can request daily temperature_min and temperature_max for the next 7 days. We need to set the timezone appropriately. The API endpoint: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast". Query parameters: latitude, longitude, daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min, timezone=America/New_York, start_date, end_date. For next week: start_date = tomorrow's date, end_date = 7 days from tomorrow? Actually next week means the upcoming 7 days. If today is e.g., 2026-05-19, next week would be 2026-05-20 to 2026-05-26 inclusive. But we don't know current date. We can compute using today's date. We'll need to get today's date. We can use Python's datetime. But we can't run code directly. We can approximate. But we can also ask the user for the date. But we can assume the current date is 2026-05-19. So next week: 2026-05-20 to 2026-05-26. We'll set start_date=2026-05-20, end_date=2026-05-26. We'll request daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min. We'll set timezone=America/New_York. We'll set temperature unit to Celsius by default. The API returns temperatures in Celsius by default. So we can call the function.

We need to produce a JSON request. The function signature: requests_get with url, headers optional, timeout optional, params with latitude, longitude, elevation optional, allow_redirects optional, auth optional, cert optional, cookies optional, proxies optional, stream optional, verify optional.
